alerts.summary: ## Description `bin/install-from-cache.js` downloads a prebuilt native addon (`*.node`) over the network and writes it directly to the artifact path **with no cryptographic integrity verification of any kind**  -  no checksum manifest, no signature, no SRI. A scan of the whole package for `createHash|sha256|checksum|integrity|digest|signature` finds nothing. The file is then `require()`-loaded by the consumer, which executes the addon's native module-init code. alerts.summary: ### Summary LLMKube's `ModelReconciler` accepts arbitrary absolute paths and `file://` URIs in the `Model.spec.source` field and propagates them to two distinct sinks without path allowlisting: (1) `os.Open()` inside the controller pod itself (`copyLocalModel`), and (2) a Kubernetes `HostPathVolumeSource` that mounts the attacker-supplied path into the inference pod's init container. Any namespace user with permission to create or update `Model` and `InferenceService` custom resources can read arbitrary files accessible to the controller pod (e.g., the controller's own Kubernetes service-account token) or arbitrary files on the node where the inference pod is scheduled (e.g., `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf`). Model caching, the feature that activates the `hostPath` sink, is **enabled by default** in both the CLI and the official Helm chart. CVSS v3.1 Base Score: **7.7 (High)**. ### Detail
alerts.title: LLMKube: Arbitrary Host File Read via Model.spec.source hostPath Injection

alerts.summary: Several tools in `mssql-mcp-core` built T-SQL by string-interpolating caller-supplied identifiers and predicates directly into the statement passed to the node-mssql `Request.query()` batch API. Only data values were parameterized. Affected tools and inputs: - `update_data`, `delete_data`: `tableName` and the free-form `whereClause` were interpolated raw. - `insert_data`: `tableName` and column names (object keys) were interpolated raw. - `execute_transaction`: the same raw `tableName`/`whereClause` interpolation per operation. - `create_table`, `create_index`, `drop_table`: table/column/index/schema identifiers were interpolated with no or insufficient validation. - `list_databases` (reader tier): the `stateFilter` argument was interpolated raw into the query, with only a non-enforced inputSchema enum guarding it.
